$comment: Tier 1 form detection parameters for the lat pulldown. DRAFT for Tony to edit. Every number is a PLACEHOLDER picked so the synthetic good rep passes and each synthetic fault fails; none is a clinical or literature value yet. Set min and/or max per check; leave both out to report the number without judging it. Feature definitions: src/pulldown/features.ts. `fault` values are Tier 1 error codes and match content/rules/tier2/lat_pulldown.yaml where that file has a code; incomplete_bottom_rom and fast_eccentric are not in it yet. lumbar_hyperextension and humeral_anterior_glide have no check: MediaPipe has no spine or scapula/humeral-head landmarks to separate them from trunk lean and shoulder movement. `variations` (Tony, 2026-10-10) changes limits for one grip variation (PULLDOWN_SETUPS id): a number replaces the shared limit, null removes it; read through pulldownParamsFor. Once the Tier 1 rule schema exists (M6a) this moves to content/rules/tier1/.

checks.why: Elbows should be close to straight at the top so the lats reach a lengthened position.
Upper arm should be well overhead at the top (shoulder flexion/abduction near end range).

Bar should come down at least to chin level. In arm lengths so it scales with the lifter (Tony, 2026-10-10): 0.32 = the old 0.18 m on the synthetic lifter's ~0.57 m arm. Loosened from 0.05 m when the bottom was redefined by the elbows reaching the trunk line (Tony, 2026-10-07).
Upper arms should finish close to the trunk (shoulder adduction/extension near end range).
At the bottom the elbows should reach the trunk line (upper arm in the trunk's frontal plane).
Stop just past the trunk line: once the whole arm rotates back around the shoulder, the extra range is shoulder hyperextension, not more lat work (Tony, 2026-10-07).
Bar should travel down a line about 12-15 deg off vertical, from ahead of the face to the upper chest (Tony, 2026-10-07). Limits padded for tracking noise.
Seen from the side, forearms should stay on the line of pull until the bottom of the rep (Tony, 2026-10-07).

Seen from the front, forearms should stay parallel to the line of pull (vertical) over the bottom 80% of the pull; the top 20% is free for the elbows to straighten (Tony, 2026-10-09). The 2.2x baseline stays within about 10-11 deg; 15 leaves room for tracking noise.
A slight lean back is normal; a big lean turns it into a row.

Trunk angle should change little within a rep; large changes mean the torso is swinging the weight. Raised from 12 to 24 when Tony's baseline swing became 18 deg (2026-10-09); the momentum swing variant is ~29.
Fast trunk extension during the pull is the signature of using momentum. Raised from 40 to 65 for the 18 deg baseline swing (good ~39 deg/s, momentum swing ~74).
Shoulders should move away from the ears (scapular depression) as the bar comes down.

The head should stay in line with the trunk instead of poking forward to meet the bar. In trunk lengths so it scales with the lifter (Tony, 2026-10-10): 0.095 = the old 0.05 m on the synthetic lifter's ~0.53 m trunk. Measured from the shoulder joints, so shoulder blade retraction also reads as head-forward (good rep up to ~0.08); forward head ~0.13+.
The bar should be lowered under control. Measured over 95%-5% of travel, so ~1.0 s here is ~1.4 s end to end.

The bar should build speed smoothly off the top, not be snapped down. Synthetic: good rep ~5 m/s2 (other faults up to 5.4), momentum swing ~8, yanked ~10. Tony (2026-10-09): a torso swing counts as a yank too.

Both hands should arrive together; a tilted bar means one side is doing less. An angle, so it holds for any grip width and body size (Tony, 2026-10-10; was 0.04 m of wrist height difference). Good reps up to ~1.1° on every grip, elbows-forward close grip ~2.7°, one side lagging 5.3°+.
Left and right elbow angles should track each other.

The bar's speed should build to one peak and ease off, on the pull and on the return; a dip in between is a sticking point or hitch (Tony, 2026-10-10). Synthetic: smooth reps up to ~16% (narrow underhand shrug ~29%), the over-pull and elbows-forward faults ~38-50% (their bar path slows near the bottom on its own), a mid-pull sticking point ~74-81%.

Reps in a set should keep the same tempo (Tony, 2026-10-10). Rep-to-rep variation of the pull or return time; synthetic steady sets ~0-4%, a set slowing 60% from first to last rep ~20%. Needs 2+ reps.
Reported only. Share of the pull's time spent on its first 25% of bar travel. Add min/max to enforce a pacing.
Reported only. Share of the pull's time spent on its middle 50% of bar travel.
Reported only. Share of the pull's time spent on its last 25% of bar travel, into the bottom.
Reported only. Share of the return's time spent leaving the bottom (first 25% of travel back up).
Reported only. Share of the return's time spent on its middle 50%.
Reported only. Share of the return's time spent reaching the stretch at the top (last 25%).

Reported only. How far the forearms leave the line of pull at the bottom; a slight break is expected (+ = elbows dropped behind the line).
Reported only. Default overhand grip is 2.0x shoulder width (Tony, 2026-10-07). MediaPipe shoulder points sit inside the acromions, so this reads slightly wide. Add a min/max to enforce a grip.

Reported only. Grip width ÷ the grip recommended from the lifter's upper arm and forearm lengths (grip.ts). 1 = on target; needs the posture-check skeleton. Add a min/max (e.g. 0.95-1.05) to enforce it.

Reported only. Shoulder width lost from top to bottom (fraction), a proxy for scapular retraction; ~0.05-0.07 on the synthetic good rep. Downward rotation has no landmark of its own and shows up as depression. Add a min to require retraction.
Reported only. Elbow angular acceleration; noisier than the wrist (second derivative of an angle). Synthetic: good ~1.5-2k, yanked ~3.7-4.4k deg/s2.
Reported only. Upper-arm angular acceleration. Does not separate a yank from a close-grip pull on synthetic data.
Reported only. Trunk lean angular acceleration; too noisy on synthetic data to judge yet.
Reported only. Most elbow bend in the rep. Add a max to cap it; a wider grip lowers it for the same bar depth.
Reported only. Degrees of arm travel about the trunk's side-to-side axis (elbows down and back from in front).
Reported only. Degrees of arm travel about the trunk's front-to-back axis (elbows down to the sides from out wide).
Reported only. 0 = pure adduction (wide frontal-plane pull), 1 = pure extension (elbows-forward sagittal pull). Add a min (e.g. 0.6) to require an extension-biased pull.
Reported only. Where the elbows point during the pull: 0 = out to the sides, 90 = straight forward. Add a min to require elbows further in front.
Reported only. Elbow ahead of the shoulder at the bottom (m); negative = behind the body.

full_stretch_at_top.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's narrow underhand baseline (2026-10-10) over 4 camera angles and 3 noise seeds (top elbow bend up to ~16°).

pull_along_line.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's narrow underhand baseline (2026-10-10) over 4 camera angles and 3 noise seeds: the close grip pulls straighter down (~4.5-6° off vertical).

forearms_on_line_front.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's narrow underhand baseline (2026-10-10) over 4 camera angles and 3 noise seeds (up to ~19°, from the elbows swinging out over the last ~15% of the pull; open question to Tony).

no_yank.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's narrow underhand baseline (2026-10-10) over 4 camera angles and 3 noise seeds (good rep up to ~7.7 m/s²; momentum swing ~12, yank ~15).

full_stretch_at_top.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's neutral bar baseline (2026-10-10, ~18:20Z) over 5 camera angles and 3 noise seeds (top elbow bend 16.9°, read up to ~18°).

elbows_reach_trunk_line.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's neutral bar baseline (2026-10-10): with the forearms on the cable the elbows stop ~12-14° in front of the trunk line. A partial pull (~-32°) still fails.

pull_along_line.why: PLACEHOLDER set around Tony's neutral bar baseline (2026-10-10): the bar comes down ~8-10° off vertical; elbows drifting forward (~19°) still fails.

no_yank.why: PLACEHOLDER set just past Tony's neutral bar baseline (2026-10-10) with his pacing on (good rep up to ~7.2 m/s²; yank ~10.4-11.5).
